problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{x+1}{(x+5)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x+5}+\frac{B}{(x+5)^{2}},
$$

find the real constants $A$ and $B.$

feedback.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{x+8}{(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x-2}+\frac{B}{(x-2)^{2}},
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are real constants, what is the value of $A\cdot B?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-2)^{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x+8 & =A(x-2)+B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=2$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2+8 & =A(2-2)+B \\ 10 & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our value for $B$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0+8 & =A(0-2)+10 \\ -2 & =-2A \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
A\cdot B=1\cdot 10=10.
$$
